retrospective.harder_than_needed: The #h Nostr group event tag uses marmotData.nostrGroupId, not the MLS group ID (MarmotGroup.idStr). This is an undocumented semantic difference that caused the AC-SNAP-1 ingest tests to fail silently until the filter was corrected to use getMarmotGroupData(state).nostrGroupId. The implementation guide did not call this out.
retrospective.surprised_by: Codex found that snapshot set() and prune() calls in selfUpdate() and commit() were not wrapped as best-effort, meaning a custom backend rejection after a relay-ACKed publish could abort state advance or Welcome delivery. The original ingest() fix only covered the prune path inside the commit-error catch; the two outbound-publish paths needed the same treatment.

implementation_summary: Implements epoch snapshot storage infrastructure for S1. Created EpochSnapshot type and EpochSnapshotStoreBackend interface in epoch-snapshot.ts. Created InMemoryEpochSnapshotStore in src/extra/. Wired snapshot calls into MarmotGroup.ingest() (AC-SNAP-1), selfUpdate() (AC-SNAP-2), and commit() (AC-SNAP-2). All snapshot set/prune calls are best-effort (try/catch with non-fatal log) so a custom backend rejection cannot abort an already-ACKed epoch transition or block Welcome delivery. Publish failure leaves state and snapshot store unchanged (AC-SNAP-3). Prune called after each advance with keepAboveEpoch = currentEpoch - snapshotDepth (AC-RET-1). Default snapshotDepth=2 (AC-RET-2, AC-STRUCT-3). destroy() calls clear() to clean up persistent snapshot backends. Plumbed snapshots/snapshotDepth through GroupsManager and MarmotClient.groupOptions. Added changeset for new public snapshot API.

reviews.codex: ran (2 rounds — findings addressed: prune-in-catch contamination, missing destroy clear(), missing changeset, best-effort wrapping for set/prune in selfUpdate and commit)
